sent_to_model:
I want to write a review of River's Edge for other movie fans. I thought it was a great movie, and there's quite a bit to discuss besides the crime itself. Can you help me put together my thoughts on the story and characters? I also want to talk about why Crispin Glover and Dennis Hopper made such an impression on me, and the connections I noticed with David Lynch's work. I'd like to give readers enough of the plot to understand my thoughts without giving away the ending. My main reason for recommending it is what it says about people staying silent when something terrible happens.

- Tim Hunter subsequently directed three episodes of Twin Peaks.
- River's Edge draws loosely from actual events; teenagers know their friend committed a killing but delay telling authorities.
- Dennis Hopper plays Feck, a middle-aged recluse selling drugs to teenagers; he has one leg.
- Samson, played by Daniel Roebuck, kills his girlfriend Jamie, played by Danyi Deats; she also belongs to his friendship group.
- Twin Peaks (1990-1991) was created by Mark Frost and David Lynch.
- Tim is played by Joshua John Miller; his older brother Matt is played by Keanu Reeves. They have a younger sister.
- Feck keeps an inflatable sex doll called Elly and converses with her.
- Layne, played by Crispin Glover, tries desperately to protect Samson; the others, even Samson himself, show little interest in his efforts.
- Alpha Dog (2006) also concerns actual events involving people knowing about a crime without reporting it.
- Feck admits killing his girlfriend previously; his motive remains uncertain, but he expresses regret and love. It doesn't seem motivated by hatred.
- Dennis Hopper also played Frank Booth in David Lynch's Blue Velvet (1986).
- Pressure builds around Samson and the group, leading to an unexpected resolution; avoid revealing the ending.
- The little sister becomes distraught about her missing doll; her mother comforts her, and Matt later helps erect a memorial cross outside.
- Tim throws his sister's doll from a bridge at the beginning; his reason is never explained.
- Samson brings his friends to see Jamie's corpse; they recoil, leave, resume ordinary activities and try to forget, without contacting police.
- After hearing shouting, Tim spots Samson beside the river, with his girlfriend's unclothed corpse nearby.
- Asked by Layne about his motive, Samson dismissively blames Jamie's insulting remarks; he shows no apparent concern about killing her.
- Hopper's performance reminded me of Blue Velvet.
- I liked Glover's performance.
- The atmosphere reminded me of David Lynch's work.
- Recommend River's Edge as an excellent film.
- Readers should recognize how readily people become indifferent, and why confronting wrongdoing matters.

(About me: amateur film reviewer. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

Discuss the characters and their reactions to events.
Assess Crispin Glover and Dennis Hopper's performances.
Discuss connections with David Lynch's work.
Recommend the film and explain its message about indifference and speaking against wrongdoing.
